newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Britain backs Romania EU bid, slams trade barriers.
newsitem.headline: Britain backs Romania EU bid, slams trade barriers.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Tuesday that London supported the opening of European markets for Romania and fellow east European states bidding for EU membership.

"Britain will champion the interests of Romania and other central and east European democracies in improving their ability to export to the European Union," Rifkind told a news conference at the end of a 24-hour visit.

"Too many European Union countries say we must maintain barriers of trade until countries like Romania are members. That is not the British view. We believe that barriers of trade must be removed and...the quicker the better."
Rifkind said Britain was "a very strong believer" in EU enlargement. Romania has an association agreement with the EU and is hoping for full membership around the year 2000.

After talks with President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, he praised the country's peaceful transfer of power after centrists threw ex-communists out of office in elections two months ago.

The new centrist coalition government is seeking financial support for a tough reform package, which underpins loan talks with the IMF, the World Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the EU.
